hero.intro: A cartridge valve screws into a machined cavity in a manifold block, so a whole circuit can live in one compact body with no pipework between the valves. Sun Hydraulics builds each function in frame sizes from series 0 to series 4; the series sets the cavity and the flow, and the configuration letters after the model code set the control, setting range, seals and material.

guidance.heading: Function first, then frame size and cavity
guidance.body: Pick the function — hold a load, limit pressure, meter flow, check or switch direction — then the flow you need, which fixes the series and the cavity. Send us the model code from the valve or the drawing, or the duty (flow, pressure, fluid and what the valve has to do), and we confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

categories.name: Counterbalance & Load-Holding Valves
categories.shortDescription: Counterbalance cartridge valves that hold a cylinder or motor load and let it down under control: 1.5:1 to 10:1 pilot ratios, standard, semi-restrictive and restrictive types, series 1 to 4.
categories.seoDescription: Sun Hydraulics counterbalance cartridge valves for cranes, booms, winches and aerial platforms: pilot ratios 1.5:1 to 10:1, vented and non-vented, series 1–4. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE.

hero.intro: A counterbalance valve sits between a cylinder or motor and its directional valve. It blocks flow out of the actuator so the load cannot run away or drift, and opens in proportion to pilot pressure from the other side of the circuit so the load comes down under control. An integral check lets free flow into the actuator.

guidance.heading: Pilot ratio, then capacity
guidance.body: Most applications run well on a 3:1 pilot ratio. A lower ratio makes the circuit more stable; a higher one needs less pilot pressure and wastes less energy, and a 10:1 valve is best avoided unless the load is very steady. Do not oversize: a counterbalance valve works on pressure drop, not flow, so the smallest capacity that passes the flow gives a stiffer, more stable circuit. Set it about 30% above the highest load-induced pressure, and choose a vented version where there is back-pressure at the inlet port, as in regeneration and proportional-valve circuits.

items.q: Why does a counterbalance valve need a higher setting than the load?
items.a: The setting must stay above the highest pressure the load can induce, so the valve never cracks open on the load alone. A common rule is about 30% above that pressure; the pilot then opens it to lower the load.

items.q: Will a counterbalance valve stop a load drifting?
items.a: Yes, when it is set correctly. The small leakage in the data is measured at reseat, about 85% of the cracking pressure; a valve set 30% above the load never sees more than about 77% of cracking, where it holds the load without drift. Cranes and man-lifts rely on this. A load that drifts through a counterbalance valve usually means a damaged seat, and the valve should be replaced.

hero.intro: Pressure-control cartridges limit or set pressure in a circuit. A relief valve caps system or line pressure; a reducing valve holds a lower pressure in a branch; a reducing/relieving valve also relieves back down to that setting; a sequence valve opens a second function only once the first has reached its pressure.

guidance.heading: Direct-acting or pilot-operated
guidance.body: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure: it is very fast, tolerant of dirt and stable, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure: its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust. Then choose the setting range that covers your working setting and the capacity for the full flow the valve may have to pass.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics 1.5:1 Pilot Ratio Counterbalance Valve — CBAB to CBIB, Series 1 to 4
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics counterbalance valve, 1.5:1 pilot ratio: CBAB to CBIB, series 1 to 4, 2.5 gpm to 120 gpm (10 L/min to 480 L/min), T-11A, T-2A, T-17A, T-19A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A counterbalance valve stops an overrunning load from running away and lowers it under control. Flow into the actuator passes freely through an integral check (port 2 to port 1). Flow out of the actuator is held by a direct-acting relief stage set above the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3, taken from the opposite side of the actuator, lowers the effective setting in proportion to the pilot ratio. Other names for it are over-centre valve and motion control valve.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 8 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • CBAB — series 1, T-11A cavity, 2.5 gpm (10 L/min), ultra-restrictive
  • CBBB — series 1, T-11A cavity, 10 gpm (40 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBCB — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBDB — series 2, T-2A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBEB — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBFB — series 3, T-17A cavity, 40 gpm (160 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBGB — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBIB — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min), standard capacity

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 1.5:1
  • Maximum setting: 4000 psi (280 bar)
  • Maximum recommended load pressure at maximum setting: 3075 psi (215 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)
  • Reseat: >85% of setting

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for CBCB; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, L — Standard Screw Adjustment, R — Lockwired Screw Adjustment
  • Setting range: A — 1000 - 4000 psi w/4 psi Check (70 - 280 bar w/ 0,3 bar Check), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, B — 400 - 1500 psi w/4 psi Check (28 - 105 bar w/ 0,3 bar Check), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, H — 1000 - 4000 psi w/25 psi Check (70 - 280 bar w/ 1,7 bar Check), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, I — 400 - 1500 psi w/25 psi Check (28 - 105 bar w/ 1,7 bar Check), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: L — Extended Temp. Buna, N — Buna-N, V — Viton
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated, /LH — Mild Steel, Zinc-Nickel

Option rules: EPDM seals are not allowed on modifier /AP or /LH; If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be L.

Selection notes

  • Set it at least 1.3 times the highest load-induced pressure.
  • Back-pressure at port 2 adds to the effective setting, multiplied by one plus the pilot ratio — use a vented version where the return line carries back-pressure.
  • Turning the adjusting screw clockwise lowers the setting and releases the load.
  • Reseats above 85% of the setting when standard set.
  • The cartridge can be screwed directly into a cavity machined in the actuator body for extra protection and stiffness.

Where it is used

Booms, jibs and winches on mobile cranes, aerial work platforms and man-lifts, drilling-rig and deck-machinery cylinders, and any actuator that can be driven by its load.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 7/8 in. (22,2 mm), 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 1: Buna: 990011007, Polyurethane: 990011002, Viton: 990011006; series 2: Buna: 990202007, Polyurethane: 990002002, Viton: 990202006, EPDM: 990202014; series 3: Buna: 990017007, Polyurethane: 990017002, Viton: 990017006; series 4: Buna: 990019007, Polyurethane: 990019002, Viton: 990019006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example CBCBLHN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics 1.5:1 Pilot Ratio Load-Reactive Load Control Valve — MBGB, MBIB, Series 3 to 4
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics load-reactive load control valve, 1.5:1 pilot ratio: MBGB, MBIB, series 3 to 4, 60 gpm to 120 gpm (240 L/min to 480 L/min), T-17A, T-19A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A 3-port load control valve that works like a counterbalance valve: an integral check gives free flow into the actuator (port 2 to port 1) and a pilot-assisted relief stage holds the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3 lowers its setting by the pilot ratio. It seats as a poppet for tight holding and meters as a spool for smooth lowering.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 2 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • MBGB — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)
  • MBIB — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 1.5:1
  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)
  • Reseat: ≥77% of setting
  • Check cracking pressure: 25 psi (1,7 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for MBIB; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: L — Standard Screw Adjustment
  • Setting range: H — 1000 - 4000 psi (70 - 280 bar), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, J — 2000 - 5000 psi (140 - 350 bar), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be L.

Selection notes

  • Set it at least 1.3 times the highest load-induced pressure, or 1.5 times where the setting is below 2,000 psi (140 bar).
  • Back-pressure at port 2 adds to the effective setting, multiplied by one plus the pilot ratio — the vented versions avoid this.
  • Turning the adjusting screw clockwise lowers the setting.

Where it is used

Load holding on large cylinders and motors in mobile and industrial machines, where higher flow is needed.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 3: Buna: 990017007, Polyurethane: 990017002, Viton: 990017006; series 4: Buna: 990019007, Polyurethane: 990019002, Viton: 990019006.

faqs.answer: Most applications run well on 3:1. A lower ratio makes a swinging or flexible load more stable; a higher ratio needs less pilot pressure and wastes less energy where the load is steady. Sun advises avoiding 10:1 unless the load is very stable.

faqs.question: Should I choose the biggest capacity that fits?
faqs.answer: No. A counterbalance valve works on pressure drop rather than flow, so the smallest frame that passes the flow gives the stiffest, most stable circuit. Oversizing tends to make the load hunt.

faqs.question: Will it stop the load drifting?
faqs.answer: Yes, when set correctly. The leakage in the data is measured at reseat, about 85% of the cracking pressure; a valve set 30% above the load never sees more than about 77% of cracking, where it holds without drift. A load that creeps through a counterbalance valve usually points to a damaged seat.

faqs.question: How high should a counterbalance valve be set?
faqs.answer: At least 1.3 times the highest pressure the load can induce, so the valve never opens on the load alone. Pilot pressure from the other side of the actuator then opens it to lower the load.

faqs.question: Which pilot ratio should I choose?
faqs.answer: Most applications run well on 3:1. A lower ratio makes a swinging or flexible load more stable; a higher ratio needs less pilot pressure and wastes less energy where the load is steady. Sun advises avoiding 10:1 unless the load is very stable.

faqs.question: Should I choose the biggest capacity that fits?
faqs.answer: No. A counterbalance valve works on pressure drop rather than flow, so the smallest frame that passes the flow gives the stiffest, most stable circuit. Oversizing tends to make the load hunt.

faqs.question: Will it stop the load drifting?
faqs.answer: Yes, when set correctly. The leakage in the data is measured at reseat, about 85% of the cracking pressure; a valve set 30% above the load never sees more than about 77% of cracking, where it holds without drift. products.descriptionLong:
A 3-port load control valve that works like a counterbalance valve: an integral check gives free flow into the actuator (port 2 to port 1) and a pilot-assisted relief stage holds the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3 lowers its setting by the pilot ratio. It seats as a poppet for tight holding and meters as a spool for smooth lowering.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 4 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • MBDA — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • MBEA — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)
  • MBGA — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)
  • MBIA — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 3:1
  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)
  • Reseat: ≥77% of setting
  • Check cracking pressure: 25 psi (1,7 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for MBDA; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, L — Standard Screw Adjustment
  • Setting range: H — 1000 - 4000 psi (70 - 280 bar), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, J — 2000 - 5000 psi (140 - 350 bar), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L.

Selection notes

  • Set it at least 1.3 times the highest load-induced pressure, or 1.5 times where the setting is below 2,000 psi (140 bar).
  • Back-pressure at port 2 adds to the effective setting, multiplied by one plus the pilot ratio — the vented versions avoid this.
  • Turning the adjusting screw clockwise lowers the setting.

Load holding on large cylinders and motors in mobile and industrial machines, where higher flow is needed.

faqs.question: How high should a counterbalance valve be set?
faqs.answer: At least 1.3 times the highest pressure the load can induce, so the valve never opens on the load alone. Pilot pressure from the other side of the actuator then opens it to lower the load.

faqs.question: Which pilot ratio should I choose?
faqs.answer: Most applications run well on 3:1. A lower ratio makes a swinging or flexible load more stable; a higher ratio needs less pilot pressure and wastes less energy where the load is steady. Sun advises avoiding 10:1 unless the load is very stable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a load control valve and a counterbalance valve?
faqs.answer: Functionally this is a 3-port counterbalance valve. It closes on a poppet seat for low leakage and modulates on a spool, which suits higher flows.

While the load is held and not yet moving, or when the load is being driven rather than overrunning, the effective pilot ratio is higher, so less pilot pressure is needed; once the load overruns, the valve controls it at its base ratio.   • Maximum setting: 4000 psi (280 bar)
  • Maximum recommended load pressure at maximum setting: 3075 psi (215 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)

Cranes, aerial platforms and handling machines that alternate between driving and lowering loads, where both stability and energy use matter.

Free flow passes into the actuator through the check (port 2 to port 1); the pilot-assisted relief stage holds the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3 lowers the setting by the pilot ratio. Circuits with back-pressure at the valve port: regeneration circuits, master–slave cylinders, and circuits driven by proportional or servo directional valves.

products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics counterbalance valve, 4.5:1 pilot ratio: CBAG to CBIG, series 1 to 4, 2.5 gpm to 120 gpm (10 L/min to 480 L/min), T-11A, T-2A, T-17A, T-19A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A counterbalance valve stops an overrunning load from running away and lowers it under control. Flow into the actuator passes freely through an integral check (port 2 to port 1). Flow out of the actuator is held by a direct-acting relief stage set above the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3, taken from the opposite side of the actuator, lowers the effective setting in proportion to the pilot ratio. Other names for it are over-centre valve and motion control valve.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 12 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • CBAG — series 1, T-11A cavity, 2.5 gpm (10 L/min), ultra-restrictive
  • CBBG — series 1, T-11A cavity, 5 gpm (20 L/min), restrictive
  • CBBD — series 1, T-11A cavity, 10 gpm (40 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBCG — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBDG — series 2, T-2A cavity, 7.5 gpm (30 L/min), restrictive
  • CBDD — series 2, T-2A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBEG — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBFG — series 3, T-17A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min), restrictive
  • CBFD — series 3, T-17A cavity, 40 gpm (160 L/min), semi-restrictive
  • CBGG — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min), standard capacity
  • CBHG — series 4, T-19A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min), restrictive
  • CBIG — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min), standard capacity

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 4.5:1
  • Maximum setting: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum recommended load pressure at maximum setting: 3850 psi (270 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)
  • Reseat: >85% of setting

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for CBCG; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: L — Standard Screw Adjustment, C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, R — Lockwired Screw Adjustment
  • Setting range: J — 2000 - 5000 psi w/25 psi Check (140 - 350 bar w/ 1,7 bar Check), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, C — 2000 - 5000 psi w/4 psi Check (140 - 350 bar w/ 0,3 bar Check), 3000 psi (210 bar) Standard Setting, D — 1000 - 2500 psi w/4 psi Check (70 - 175 bar w/ 0,3 bar Check), 2000 psi (140 bar) Standard Setting, K — 1000 - 2500 psi w/25 psi Check (70 - 175 bar w/ 1,7 bar Check), 2000 psi (140 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, L — Buna (low temp), V — Viton, E — EPDM
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated, /LH — Mild Steel, Zinc-Nickel

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C, L or R; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be C or L; If the seal is E, the control must be C or L.

Selection notes

  • Set it at least 1.3 times the highest load-induced pressure.
  • Back-pressure at port 2 adds to the effective setting, multiplied by one plus the pilot ratio — use a vented version where the return line carries back-pressure.
  • Turning the adjusting screw clockwise lowers the setting and releases the load.
  • Reseats above 85% of the setting when standard set.
  • The cartridge can be screwed directly into a cavity machined in the actuator body for extra protection and stiffness.

Where it is used

Booms, jibs and winches on mobile cranes, aerial work platforms and man-lifts, drilling-rig and deck-machinery cylinders, and any actuator that can be driven by its load.

(41,3 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). faqs.question: How high should a counterbalance valve be set?
faqs.answer: At least 1.3 times the highest pressure the load can induce, so the valve never opens on the load alone. Pilot pressure from the other side of the actuator then opens it to lower the load.

faqs.question: Which pilot ratio should I choose?
faqs.answer: Most applications run well on 3:1. A lower ratio makes a swinging or flexible load more stable; a higher ratio needs less pilot pressure and wastes less energy where the load is steady. Sun advises avoiding 10:1 unless the load is very stable.

faqs.question: Should I choose the biggest capacity that fits?
faqs.answer: No. A counterbalance valve works on pressure drop rather than flow, so the smallest frame that passes the flow gives the stiffest, most stable circuit. Oversizing tends to make the load hunt.

faqs.question: Will it stop the load drifting?
faqs.answer: Yes, when set correctly. The leakage in the data is measured at reseat, about 85% of the cracking pressure; a valve set 30% above the load never sees more than about 77% of cracking, where it holds without drift. A load that creeps through a counterbalance valve usually points to a damaged seat.

products.descriptionLong:
A 3-port load control valve that works like a counterbalance valve: an integral check gives free flow into the actuator (port 2 to port 1) and a pilot-assisted relief stage holds the load (port 1 to port 2) until pilot pressure at port 3 lowers its setting by the pilot ratio. It seats as a poppet for tight holding and meters as a spool for smooth lowering.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 3 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • MBEGX — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)
  • MBGGX — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)
  • MBIGX — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 4.5:1
  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)
  • Reseat: ≥77% of setting
  • Check cracking pressure: 25 psi (1,7 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for MBIGX; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Setting range: K — 3000 psi (210 bar), L — 4000 psi (280 bar), M — 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton

Selection notes

Load holding on large cylinders and motors in mobile and industrial machines, where higher flow is needed.

products.descriptionLong:
A self-setting counterbalance valve. Instead of a fixed setting it moves its working setting to roughly 1.3× the pressure the load induces, capped by a fixed thermal relief setting, and combines reverse free flow, load control and thermal relief in one cartridge. Because the working setting is only as high as the load needs, it usually opens with less pilot pressure than a conventional valve with the same relief setting.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 2 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • MBDP — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • MBEP — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 drops/min. (0,3 cc/min)

  • Check cracking pressure: 25 psi (1,7 bar)

  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be D.

Selection notes

Mobile machines whose loads vary widely, where lower pilot pressure saves energy and fuel.

products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-to-open load control valve with a balanced modulating element and a reverse-flow check. Free flow passes into the actuator through the check (port 2 to port 1); flow out of the actuator is metered by pilot pressure at port 3, and because the element is balanced against load pressure the flow stays steady as the load changes.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.

faqs.question: Will it fit the same cavity as my existing relief cartridge?
faqs.answer: Sun's 2-port relief cartridges of one frame size share the same cavity and flow path, so a direct-acting and a pilot-operated relief of the same series are interchangeable. Pilot-capacity reliefs are the exception — check the cavity in the size table.

A pilot-operated relief that behaves like a circuit breaker. It resets only when flow stops and the pressure at port 2 equals or exceeds that at port 1.

  • RQGB — series 2, T-3A cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)
  • RQIB — series 3, T-16A cavity, 100 gpm (380 L/min)
  • RQKB — series 4, T-18A cavity, 200 gpm (760 L/min)

faqs.answer: Stop the flow through the valve and let the pressure at port 2 equal or exceed port 1, usually by shifting the directional valve to neutral.

faqs.question: Can I use a kick-down relief as my system relief?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. It does not regulate pressure; keep a normal relief for system protection.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.

faqs.question: Will it fit the same cavity as my existing relief cartridge?
faqs.answer: Sun's 2-port relief cartridges of one frame size share the same cavity and flow path, so a direct-acting and a pilot-operated relief of the same series are interchangeable. Pilot-capacity reliefs are the exception — check the cavity in the size table.

products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics relief main stage with integral T-8A pilot cavity: RPEC8, RPGC8, RPKC8, series 1 to 4, 25 gpm to 200 gpm (95 L/min to 760 L/min), T-10A, T-3A, T-18A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated relief main stage with its own T-8A control cavity machined into the cartridge. Any T-8A pressure-control cartridge screwed into that cavity sets the relief pressure — a manual pilot relief, an electro-proportional pilot, or an air-controlled one — so the same main stage can be adjusted locally or controlled remotely.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 3 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • RPEC8 — series 1, T-10A cavity, 25 gpm (95 L/min)
  • RPGC8 — series 2, T-3A cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)
  • RPKC8 — series 4, T-18A cavity, 200 gpm (760 L/min)

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for RPEC8; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Setting range: D — 25 - 3000 psi (1,7 - 210 bar), W — 100 - 5000 psi (7 - 350 bar)
  • Seal material: L — Extended Temp. Buna, N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Selection notes

  • Supplied as the main stage; the T-8A pilot cartridge is chosen separately.
  • The pilot cartridge's setting determines the pressure difference across the valve.

Where it is used

Building remotely or electronically controlled relief functions without a separate pilot body.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 7/8 in. (22,2 mm), 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 1: Buna: 990010007, EPDM: 990010014, Polyurethane: 990010002, Viton: 990010006; series 2: Buna: 990203007, EPDM: 990203014, Polyurethane: 990003002, Viton: 990203006; series 4: Buna: 990018007, EPDM: 990018014, Polyurethane: 990018002, Viton: 990018006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example RPEC8WN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

products.descriptionLong:
A normally closed, pilot-operated relief cartridge with a balanced piston main stage. A small pilot stage senses pressure at port 1; when it reaches the setting the main stage opens to tank at port 2 and throttles flow to regulate pressure. It holds its setting closely as flow increases, runs smooth and quiet, and responds moderately fast.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 5 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • RPCC — series 0, T-162A cavity, 12 gpm (45 L/min), 0-series
  • RPEC — series 1, T-10A cavity, 25 gpm (95 L/min)
  • RPGC — series 2, T-3A cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)
  • RPIC — series 3, T-16A cavity, 100 gpm (380 L/min)
  • RPKC — series 4, T-18A cavity, 200 gpm (760 L/min)

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 2 in³/min.@1000 psi (30 cc/min.@70 bar), 3 in³/min.@1000 psi (50 cc/min.@70 bar), 4 in³/min.@1000 psi (65 cc/min.@70 bar), 5 in³/min.@1000 psi (80 cc/min.@70 bar)
  • Typical response time: 10 ms

Configuration options

  • Setting range: A — 100 - 3000 psi (7 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, W — 150 - 4500 psi (10,5 - 315 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, B — 50 - 1500 psi (3,5 - 105 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, C — 150 - 6000 psi (10,5 - 420 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, N — 60 - 800 psi (4 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, Q — 60 - 400 psi (4 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, D — 25 - 800 psi (1,7 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, E — 25 - 400 psi (1,7 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, G — 60 - 3000 psi (4 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, H — 30 - 3000 psi (2 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, K — 75 - 1500 psi (5 - 105 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, P — 40 - 400 psi (2,8 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, V — 150 - 800 psi (10,5 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be C or L; If the seal is E, the control must be C,K,L,R,O,W or Y.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.

faqs.question: Will it fit the same cavity as my existing relief cartridge?
faqs.answer: Sun's 2-port relief cartridges of one frame size share the same cavity and flow path, so a direct-acting and a pilot-operated relief of the same series are interchangeable. Pilot-capacity reliefs are the exception — check the cavity in the size table.

faqs.question: Can it be used as a cross-port relief?
faqs.answer: Yes. The valve accepts full system pressure at port 2, so two of them can protect both sides of a motor or cylinder. With spool-type stages, allow for their leakage in a cross-port circuit.

faqs.question: What does venting a relief valve do?
faqs.answer: Connecting the vent port to tank lets the main stage open at low pressure, so the pump unloads without stopping. A pilot relief on the vent port gives a second, lower setting instead.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.

products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated relief cartridge with a vent port (port 3) connected between the main stage and its pilot. Opening the vent to tank unloads the pump at low pressure; connecting a remote pilot relief to it gives a lower, remotely adjusted setting; a 2-way valve on the vent switches between the two. It is accurate, smooth and quiet, with low pressure rise as flow increases.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 4 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • RVCS — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • RVES — series 2, T-2A cavity, 25 gpm (95 L/min)
  • RVGS — series 3, T-17A cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)
  • RVIS — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 10 drops/min. (0,7 cc/min)
  • Typical response time: 2 ms

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for RVCS; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, K — Handknob, L — Standard Screw Adjustment
  • Setting range: A — 100 - 3000 psi (7 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, B — 50 - 1500 psi (3,5 - 105 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, C — 150 - 6000 psi (10,5 - 420 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, N — 60 - 800 psi (4 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, Q — 60 - 400 psi (4 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, W — 150 - 4500 psi (10,5 - 315 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated, /LH — Mild Steel, Zinc-Nickel

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be C or L; If the seal is E, the control must be C,K or L.

Selection notes

  • A remote pilot relief on the vent port controls the valve below its own setting.
  • Accepts full pressure at port 2.

Where it is used

Pump unloading, remote pressure setting and two-pressure circuits on power units and presses.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 7/8 in. (22,2 mm), 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 1: Buna: 990611007, Viton: 990611006; series 2: Buna: 990402007, Polyurethane: 990002002, Viton: 990402006; series 3: Buna: 990217007, Polyurethane: 990217002, Viton: 990217006; series 4: Buna: 990219007, Viton: 990219006.

Ordering

faqs.question: What does venting a relief valve do?
faqs.answer: Connecting the vent port to tank lets the main stage open at low pressure, so the pump unloads without stopping. A pilot relief on the vent port gives a second, lower setting instead.

faqs.question: Direct-acting or pilot-operated relief — which one?
faqs.answer: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure and shock: it is very fast and tolerant of dirt, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure, because its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust.
